constituent

/kuhn-STICH-oo-uhnt/ - the stress falls on STICH · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Constituent means an essential part of a whole.

Nitrogen is the chief constituent of the air we breathe, nearly four-fifths of every lungful.

Example

At the stone yard, the guide hands each visitor a hand lens and a slab of granite. Look closely, he says, and the speckles sharpen into three constituents: glassy grey quartz, blocky pink feldspar, and small dark flakes of mica that catch the light. Granite is not one rock but a partnership, and it behaves like one — heat it, and each mineral answers differently.

Constituent is the exact word for each of those three, because it names an essential part of a whole. Take away the quartz, the feldspar, or the mica and what remains is no longer granite; a constituent is the kind of part whose absence changes what the whole thing is.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

ingredient: Ingredient is the kitchen's word — a part measured and stirred into the dish or the recipe. A constituent is found by analysis rather than added by hand: the quartz in granite, the nitrogen in air, a part so essential the whole is not itself without it.

element: An element is one of the basic parts something contains — an element of a plan, of a crime, of a style — and it stays neutral about importance. A constituent makes the stronger claim: this part is essential, and removing it changes what the whole is.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

whole: the complete thing itself, not a part of it

add-on: a tacked-on extra the whole never needed

Where it sits · how much the whole depends on it — component → constituent → cornerstone

component vs. constituent: A component is any part on the parts list — a tire is a component of a car, and so is the ashtray — while a constituent is a part the whole cannot be itself without.

cornerstone vs. constituent: Cornerstone goes past constituent — not just an essential part but the one part everything else is built around.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: together

Root — stitu-

Root — stitu-: to set up, to place (Latin statuere)

Suffix — -ent

Suffix — -ent: that which does

Put it together

Put it together: Con- (together) + stitu- (to set up) + -ent (that which) = that which is set up together. Latin constituere meant to establish, to set in place; the constituents are the parts set together to make the whole stand. The political sense is the same picture: the voters of a district are the parts that, set together, constitute it.

Use the root in a new word: statue

Use the root in a new word: statue: A statue shares the root: a figure set up to stand in its place, often for centuries.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / technical

Constituent is the chemist's and analyst's word: it insists the part is essential to what the whole is. Component is looser — any listed part — and ingredient stays in the kitchen. In politics, a constituent is a person a representative serves: the same root idea, one of the parts that together make up the district. This card's sense is the part, not the voter.
